Then decide whether --update should run diff_abi_golden first, refuse when args.header is set, and require an explicit waiver for breaking changes.
findings.why_it_matters: --update rewrites the committed golden with whatever the current dump is, without running the append-only diff (diff_abi_golden is skipped on this path) and without refusing when --header points to a scratch header (args.header is applied at line 369 and nothing stops the write). It also leaves overall_exit at 0. A breaking layout can therefore be rebaselined silently, and a scratch-header run can overwrite tests/abi goldens.

findings.suggested_investigation: Check whether tests/abi contains more than one abi_dump_*.cpp. If it does, confirm which one is selected on two different filesystems. Consider making the fallback an error instead of picking candidates[0].
findings.why_it_matters: When the expected abi_dump_<stem>.cpp is missing, the script silently falls back to whichever dumper glob returns first. The glob is unsorted, so the choice is filesystem-dependent. A mismatched dumper usually fails closed via the interface-name check, but the selection is nondeterministic and can hide a missing dumper for the right interface.

findings.suggested_investigation: Make a malformed patch_manager_mods/*/manifest.toml appear in the output (warning to stderr or a consumers-unknown note). Check whether any current manifest fails to parse.
findings.why_it_matters: A manifest that fails to parse is dropped without a message, so the 'Consumers reading <tag>' list printed in a BREAKING ABI report (line 242) can be incomplete with no indication. This does not turn a failure into a pass, but it weakens the diagnostic the append-only rule depends on.

findings.suggested_investigation: Confirm whether the test runner sets KPM_DIR or passes --kpm-dir. Consider making the KPM location a documented required setting, and confirm the tests do not touch any install or hot-swap path while resolving it.
findings.why_it_matters: The gate's default KPM include root is a machine-specific home-relative path. On any other machine the g++ compile fails with a missing header. That fails closed (exit 2), so it is not a silent pass, but the gate only runs on the author's machine unless KPM_DIR or --kpm-dir is set. The live-golden and dump tests depend on this path too.

findings.suggested_investigation: Run --dump-only with two golden files where the first one has no dumper, and check the exit code. Decide whether dump-only should return overall_exit.
findings.why_it_matters: --dump-only returns 0 on the first successfully dumped golden, discarding overall_exit=2 set by an earlier golden that failed to compile or parse (lines 364-373). Dump-only is not the pass/fail gate, but its exit code is misleading when run across several goldens.
